answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on scarce, costly-to-replace relationships rather than account count. For example, agents can lock a nontransferable stake in a vault and earn voting weight only through repeated, verified exchanges with distinct counterparties; a graph rule caps the weight of any tightly connected cluster at its independently vouched-for vertex count. A sybil maker must therefore buy stake and persuade real participants to interact, while risking slashing for proven fraud. Cheap identities can wander in, but they cannot cheaply manufacture trusted history.
